answer:
**A confident softmax can simply mean one class score is much larger than the others.** It does not directly say whether the input resembles training data or whether another plausible model would disagree. A model can be confidently wrong on an unfamiliar input. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/calibration.html) [3](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book2.html)

Deep ensembles train multiple models and compare their predictions. MC dropout samples predictions with stochastic dropout active. If members confidently choose different classes, their average can reveal disagreement that one model's softmax hides.

**Agreement is not proof of knowledge.** Models can share architecture, data, and blind spots, so every member may make the same unsupported prediction. Evidential approaches parameterize uncertainty over class probabilities but also depend on training assumptions and can fail under shift.

Evaluate calibration, out-of-distribution behavior, and risk–coverage curves: as uncertain cases are deferred, does the error rate on retained cases fall? Compare entropy of the average with average member entropy to separate some disagreement from shared ambiguity under the chosen approximation. Treat uncertainty estimates as signals to validate, not automatic certificates of reliability.

**Technical details and references.**

A softmax score describes relative class preference under one fitted model; it does not directly measure how uncertain the model is about its parameters or unsupported inputs. Deep ensembles approximate model disagreement, while MC dropout samples predictions under stochastic dropout. Both can provide useful uncertainty signals but require calibration and out-of-distribution evaluation. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/calibration.html) [3](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book2.html)

For classification, compare entropy of the mean predictive distribution with mean member entropy; their difference estimates disagreement under the chosen approximation. Evidential models parameterize distributions over class probabilities, but their uncertainty depends on training assumptions and can be overconfident under shift. Evaluate risk–coverage curves, calibration, and abstention behavior. Neither a single low-confidence score nor ensemble agreement establishes that a prediction is reliable outside the data-generating regime.
